title: What time is it?
summary: Ask and tell the time, with half past, quarter past and quarter to.
intro: To ask the time, say كَمِ السَّاعَة؟ (literally 'how much is the hour?'). Answer with السَّاعَة and a feminine 'first, second, third' word: السَّاعَة الثَّالِثَة (three o'clock). Add وَالنِّصْف for half past, وَالرُّبْع for quarter past and إِلَّا رُبْعًا for quarter to.
objectives: Tell the time on the hour from one to ten o'clock
Add half past, quarter past and quarter to
Say when something happens with فِي السَّاعَة …

realLife.title: Late for class
realLife.story: Daniel's phone battery is dead, so his alarm does not ring, and the bus is slow. He runs into class at quarter past nine. Mr Karim is kind about it, but now Daniel really wants a watch.

mistakes.why: For the time, use 'the third' (ath-thālitha), not the counting word 'three'.

sentences.literal: the hour (is) the tenth and the half

sentences.en: The lesson is at nine o'clock in the morning.
sentences.literal: the lesson (is) at the hour the ninth in the morning
the hour (is) the second minus a quarter

mistakes.why: After illā the word takes the -an ending: illā rubʿan.

dialogue.title: Quarter past nine
dialogue.culture: In Egyptian everyday speech you will hear السَّاعَة كَام؟ for 'what time is it?', but in Modern Standard Arabic the question is كَمِ السَّاعَة؟. Times for meeting friends are often loose: 'at nine' can mean a little after nine.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا أُسْتَاذ! أَنَا آسِف جِدًّا، أَنَا مُتَأَخِّر.
lines.en: Good morning, sir! I am very sorry, I am late.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور يَا دَانْيَال. كَمِ السَّاعَة الْآن، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: Good morning, Daniel. What time is it now, please?

lines.ar: عَفْوًا يَا أُسْتَاذ، هَاتِفِي بِدُونِ بَطَّارِيَّة الْيَوْم.
lines.en: Excuse me, sir, my phone has no battery today.

lines.ar: السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة وَالرُّبْع. الدَّرْس فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة بِالضَّبْط!
lines.en: It is quarter past nine. The lesson is at exactly nine o'clock!

lines.ar: نَعَم، أَعْرِفُ. وَالْحَافِلَة الْيَوْم بَطِيئَة جِدًّا!
lines.en: Yes, I know. And the bus is very slow today!

lines.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. تَفَضَّلْ، اِجْلِسْ. الدَّرْس الْيَوْم عَنِ الْوَقْت!
lines.en: No problem. Please, sit down. Today's lesson is about time!

lines.ar: هٰذَا دَرْس مُهِمّ لَكَ يَا دَانْيَال!
lines.en: This is an important lesson for you, Daniel!

lines.ar: يَا لَيْلَى، كَمِ السَّاعَة عَلَى سَاعَتِكِ؟
lines.en: Layla, what time is it on your watch?

lines.ar: السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة وَالرُّبْع يَا أُسْتَاذ. وَمَتَى الاِسْتِرَاحَة الْيَوْم؟
lines.en: It is quarter past nine, sir. And when is the break today?

lines.ar: الاِسْتِرَاحَة فِي السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة وَالنِّصْف، وَالدَّرْس حَتَّى السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة.
lines.en: The break is at half past ten, and the lesson goes on until one o'clock.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدَ الدَّرْس؟ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ وَقْت لِلْقَهْوَة؟
lines.en: And after the lesson? Do you all have time for a coffee?

lines.ar: نَعَم، لٰكِنْ فِي السَّاعَة الثَّالِثَة عِنْدِي مَوْعِد مَعَ مُدِيرِ الْمَدْرَسَة.
lines.en: Yes, but at three o'clock I have an appointment with the head of the school.

lines.ar: إِذَنْ، الْقَهْوَة فِي السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة وَالنِّصْف. عِنْدَكَ وَقْت كَثِير!
lines.en: Then coffee at half past one. You have plenty of time!

lines.ar: وَيَا دَانْيَال، اِشْتَرِ سَاعَة جَدِيدَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ!
lines.en: And Daniel, please buy yourself a new watch!

lines.ar: فِكْرَة مُمْتَازَة! غَدًا أَنَا فِي الصَّفّ فِي السَّاعَة الثَّامِنَة وَالنِّصْف.
lines.en: Excellent idea! Tomorrow I'll be in class at half past eight.

reading.title: My school day
reading.ar: الدَّرْس فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة صَبَاحًا، وَالاِسْتِرَاحَة فِي السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة وَالنِّصْف. يَوْمَ الْخَمِيس الدَّرْس حَتَّى السَّاعَة الرَّابِعَة. وَفِي الْمَسَاء، مِنَ السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة إِلَى السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة، أَدْرُسُ فِي الْبَيْت.
reading.en: The lesson is at nine o'clock in the morning, and the break is at half past ten. On Thursday the lesson goes on until four o'clock. In the evening, from six to seven o'clock, I study at home.

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'It is five o'clock'?
In the dialogue, what time does Daniel arrive?
Which word has the th sound of 'think'?

completion: Great work! You can ask كَمِ السَّاعَة؟ and tell the time to the nearest quarter of an hour.
